question: Does a typed flow-source completion of Q24 avoid an equilibrium artifact, and can local circulation excite the harmonic graphite port?

objects.object_type: positive stock probability in candidate CTMC

objects.definition: Q24 with proposed w_ij=T_ij and Xi_ij=sigma_ij=-sigma_ji
objects.units: eta_O per internal time; graphite units absent

objects.exact_expression: B1J=0; M^T J=0 when B2^T M=0
objects.normalization: integer face coefficients, M constant harmonic columns

sources.source_status: Q24 conditional, Q25/Q26 open; support continuity does not supply Markov rates
separately declared contact gate; no graphite route rates
conditional positive-stock construction; no graphite identification

assumptions: A1 finite candidate CTMC with exogenous nonnegative rates and internal dimensionless time
A2 Q24 w is traffic and Xi fixed signed orientation, not current canon
A3 face current mapped to B2 f in unit-metric honeycomb quotient; Q24 c not automatically this chain

technique_plan.purpose_or_na_reason: prove sum conservation, stationarity and detailed-balance distinction
two-state false source and three-state circulation witness
B1B2=0 and B2^T M=0 on N7/13/19
no count divisibility or finite cyclic update is used

factor_origins: declared rates 2,1 and normalized p; no target fitting

dynamics_readout.state_space: probability simplex over finite graph and signed edge current; separate honeycomb chain spaces
dynamics_readout.generator_or_update: positive Markov generator, rates externally declared
dynamics_readout.initial_boundary_conditions: closed finite graph and stationary examples; toroidal quotient for projection
dynamics_readout.conservation_and_sources: sum p=1, p>=0; J antisymmetric; three-cycle has circulating current
dynamics_readout.projection_and_kernel: face-boundary current im B2 is orthogonal to harmonic ker B1 intersect ker B2^T
dynamics_readout.physical_mapping: eta_O energy scale, physical time, C/K/D, contact and force OPEN

target_exposure.search_domain_and_budget: single flow-typed Markov completion and two exact counterexamples; exponential speed family illustrative
target_exposure.selection_criterion: detect equilibrium artifact and test harmonic reachability
target_exposure.baseline: conventional PES/contact and prior source parity

calculation_steps: CTMC generator conserves total p; directed traffic p_i k_ij differs from bare rate k_ij.
For two states rates 2,1, stationary p=(1/3,2/3); traffic=(2/3,2/3), so c_traffic=0 while c_rate=1/2 at eta=sigma=1.
For three-state ring rates a=2,b=1, uniform p=1/3 is stationary, J=1/3 and c=1/6.
For honeycomb face J=B2f, B1J=0 by boundary-square; M^T J=(B2^T M)^T f=0.
For smooth a=r exp(zeta u/2), b=r exp(-zeta u/2), c=eta sigma r sinh(zeta u/2)/3 with linear coefficient eta sigma r zeta/6.

result.exact_expression: c=eta sigma J/2; J=0 at detailed balance; M^T B2 f=0
result.approximation: small dimensionless speed u Taylor only
result.units: internal rate multiplied by unknown eta; no graphite force units
result.precision_and_error: exact rational/integer checks and symbolic identities; physical uncertainty NOT_AVAILABLE
result.scope: candidate Markov source and unit-metric periodic honeycomb carrier

verification.method: exact fraction and integer incidence replay

counterexamples_and_failures: Bare rates yield nonzero Q24 at reversible two-state equilibrium, so rate and traffic must not be conflated.
A stationary three-state cycle has nonzero current despite dp/ds=0; stationarity alone is not detailed balance.
Nonzero face current B2 f has zero harmonic projection, so a local circulation alone cannot be the harmonic port input.
Exchange-even route, static bias, noncontractible winding or different cross-Hessian map evade the narrow conclusions.
limitations: Markov irreversibility and rates are proposed, not derived from UD skew support
Q24 c and signed J have different types; no automatic port identification
no N7 selectivity, material coefficient or experimental residual
next_discriminant: obtain actual packet-derived route/rates and registered graphite material response; test noncontractible winding plus source/bath across N7/13/19
